Server side favours server-sent events, and Spring itself says so.
An SSE endpoint is one controller method returning `SseEmitter` with `produces=text/event-stream`, writing events in the standard format, with async support enabled and a timeout configured.
With `spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true`, a blocked write per idle connection costs a virtual thread rather than a platform thread.
The HTML standard defines `id:`, `retry:`, and the `Last-Event-ID` request header, so "give me everything after this cursor" is a header on the reconnect request the server already handles.
OpenAPI 3.2.0, released 2025, added sequential media types and `itemSchema`, which describes each event of an event stream independently.
The same document can describe the REST API and the stream.
Generating a WebSocket client from a description is not a supported path today.
The JDK ships a `WebSocket` client and no `EventSource`, so the JavaFX, tray, and CLI clients each need a small SSE reader: a line parser, the `Last-Event-ID` header, and backoff.
"Server-sent events reconnect automatically" is a browser `EventSource` property, not a wire guarantee, so the reconnect path is hand-written either way.
What this task does not decide: `live-api-choice` decides.
